title: Depth-Bounds for Neural Networks via the Braid Arrangement

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The abstract claims an “unconditional” Omega(log log d) lower bound for “general ReLU networks” and says the open question is “completely” resolved. But the actual theorem proved in Section 4 is explicitly only for B_d^0-conforming networks, i.e. networks whose intermediate breakpoints are restricted to the braid arrangement. The conclusion directly acknowledges this: “We established a doubly-logarithmic lower bound under the assumption that breakpoints lie on the braid fan” and says the bound “may not extend to all networks.” Thus the abstract and introductory claims materially overstate the result.

The abstract says that “arbitrary neural networks require three hidden layers to compute the maximum of 5 numbers.” In contrast, the Introduction states that Bakaev et al. [2025b] “showed that two hidden layers are sufficient to represent max{0, x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4},” which is the maximum of five numbers. The Conclusion repeats this two-layer general-network result. Section 5 proves only a lower bound for B_d^0-conforming networks, not arbitrary networks.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph beginning “In Section 4 we prove for d = ...”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: It states that “all continuous piecewise linear functions on R^d require depth Omega(log log d) for exact representation.” This is false literally: affine functions, constants, and many other CPWL functions require no hidden layers. The Section 4 argument at most establishes that one particular function (a maximum) is excluded from a restricted conforming architecture at a given depth.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, first paragraph under the NeurIPS header
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper attributes to Cybenko [1989] and Hornik [1991] the result that ReLU networks “compute exactly the class of continuous piecewise linear (CPWL) functions.” Those papers concern universal approximation with sigmoidal/general activations, not exact characterization of finite ReLU-network functions as CPWL nor exact representation of every CPWL function by ReLU networks. The following paragraph attributes the relevant exact-ReLU result to Arora et al. [2018], which underscores the misattribution.

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition 2.1 and the immediately following description of the braid fan
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Definition 2.1 defines B_d using both x_i=x_j and x_i=0 hyperplanes, i.e. the extended braid arrangement. Such a fan has trivial lineality space, because the coordinate-zero hyperplanes eliminate the span of the all-ones vector. Immediately afterward the paper asserts that B_d has lineality span(1_[d]) and gives cones of the form cone(1_S1,...,1_Sk)+span(1_[d]), which are the cones of the ordinary braid fan containing only x_i=x_j hyperplanes. The subsequent definition of B_d^0 repeats the same hyperplanes already assigned to B_d. These incompatible definitions invalidate the claimed quotient relation and the later B_d/B_d^0 translations.

predicted_errors.error_location: Propositions 2.2 and 2.3, especially the asserted basis {sigma_M | M subseteq [d]} and formula for Phi
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Under the paper's definition, V_{B_d} contains arbitrary constants: the constant function 1 is CPWL and compatible with every fan. Yet sigma_empty is defined as max_{i in empty} x_i, which is undefined. If it is tacitly interpreted as zero, then the stated formula Phi(sum_M lambda_M sigma_M)(S)=sum_{M: M intersect S nonempty} lambda_M always gives value 0 at S=empty, so it cannot represent Phi(1)(empty)=1. Hence the alleged basis, isomorphism, inverse formula, and dimension statements cannot all hold for the stated space. A constant basis element or an explicit restriction to homogeneous functions normalized at zero would be needed.

Lemma 4.4(1) claims alpha_{X,Y} lies in the span of alpha_{S,S union T} for “S supseteq Y minus T.” This is inconsistent with the required form of those sublattices and with the examples and later text, which use S subseteq Y minus T. For example, with X=empty, Y={a,b,c,d}, and T={a,b,c}, the displayed decomposition uses S=empty and S={d}; neither satisfies S supseteq Y minus T={d} in the first case. As written, the span condition is wrong and cannot support the subsequent induction.

predicted_errors.error_location: Corollary 4.9 versus the Section 4 opening paragraph and Theorem 4.8
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 4 says the intended excluded target is max{0,x_1,...,x_{2^{2^ell-1}}}. This follows from Theorem 4.8, whose bound is V_{B_d}(2^{2^ell-1}): to exclude the full-set maximum one needs one more braid-fan coordinate. Corollary 4.9 instead writes x maps to {0,x_1,...,x_{2^{2^ell}-1}}, changing the exponent from 2^ell-1 to 2^ell and placing the final −1 outside the exponent. It also omits the max operator. This is not the stated consequence of Theorem 4.8.

Theorem 5.2 states M^2_{B_d^0}(2) = V_{B_d}(4). These are spaces defined using different fans: the left-hand side consists of B_d^0-conforming network functions, whereas the right-hand side was defined as functions compatible with B_d. The earlier Lemma 3.1 only gives an equivalence after changing from R^{d-1} to R^d and changing the target max function; it does not justify this equality as written. Given the already contradictory definitions of B_d and B_d^0, this is additionally ill-typed/ambiguous.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph beginning “Understanding depth lower bounds is crucial because...”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text claims that proving lower bounds for max “completely resolves the mystery of why max-pooling layers are essential” and proves shallow ReLU stacks “inferior in all practical scenarios.” No such practical or universal architectural conclusion follows from an exact-representation lower bound for one function, especially one proved only under a braid-conformity restriction. This is a substantial unsupported extrapolation.

Section 2 promises “Appendix A” for notation and “Appendix B” for “detailed proofs of all the statements.” The supplied full paper contains neither Appendix A nor Appendix B; after the Appendix heading it contains only acknowledgments and references. Central results are therefore left as assertions or proof sketches, including Proposition 6.1, while the promised detailed proofs are absent.
